subject: Renewal: aligning term + surge lanes for upcoming expansion
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestline.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Morris <procurement@crestline.ai>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@finance.crestline.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase for Q3 rollout

Sean —

Hope you're well. We're starting planning for a bigger Q3 rollout of our assistant product and expect a ~3x increase in inference spend across the next 12 months. Our subscription with Redwood is coming up for renewal in July and we want to:

- align the term with our fiscal year (multi-year is on the table)
- add surge lanes & a predictable ramp schedule (we need guaranteed burst capacity for launches)
- understand auto-renew and co-term options so we can simplify procurement renewals across multiple vendors

I'm attaching our internal renewal request and a sketch of projected token consumption. Could you share what a few practical renewal structures look like (multi-year discounts, staged ramp with true-up, invoice cadence)? Also want to make sure there is an ops-safe canary path in case we need a step-increase mid-quarter.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform
Crestline AI

Attachments: Crestline_Renewal_Request.pdf (pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase for Q3 rollout

Hi Liam —

Great context, thanks for the deck. High-level options we see that balance predictability and cost:

1) Multi-year locked term (24 months) + graduated ramp
   - 12% discount off list on committed capacity
   - ramp schedule: 1.0x (Q1), 1.6x (Q2), 3.0x (Q3 onward) with quarterly true-ups
   - invoice cadence: quarterly in arrears (option to annual prepay for additional 4% discount)

2) 12-month commitment with surge lanes (preferred for fast launches)
   - lower commitment discount (7%) + guaranteed burst pool (pre-provisioned GPUs)
   - step-in credits for one unplanned surge per year (up to 2x for a single week)

3) Co-term + auto-renew model (for portfolio simplicity)
   - co-terming across multiple Redwood accounts; single renewal notice, auto-renew opt-out window (30 days)
   - can include a canary deploy quota that allows gradual traffic shift to new model variants during rollout

I've attached an option matrix with illustrative numbers (Redwood_Option_Matrix_Q2-27.xlsx) and a draft amendment that maps to option 1 and option 2 constructs.

Operational notes:
- Canary path: we recommend a 14-day canary with a reserved 10% burst lane and automatic fallback to validated model variant.
- Ramp true-ups should be driven off token metrics emitted to your billing export (we can add a token-level delta webhook).

Next steps: if you like option 1 or 2, we'll route pricing and legal and produce a clean amendment for signature. Marissa/ Karthik — could you review the matrix and flag anything we should surface to finance/legal?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_Option_Matrix_Q2-27.xlsx (xlsx), Proposed_AMENDMENT_v2.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase for Q3 rollout

Sean —

Thanks, read quickly and these are my recommended guardrails before we send a formal proposal to Crestline:

- Prefer option 1 for 24 months with quarterly true-ups. Locks revenue and surfaces predictable uplift; offer an early upsell credit (one-time onboarding credit) tied to successful Q3 launch metrics.
- Keep surge lanes as a paid add-on but include one complimentary short-duration surge for launch (48 hours).
- In the amendment: remove automatic unlimited step-in credits; instead define a 2-tier surge process (pre-approved burst pool + emergency step-in with additional fees).
- Co-term: accept co-terming but make auto-renew opt-in default with explicit opt-out window (30 days). That reduces churn risk.

I'll draft the pricing appendix with the exact numbers (discount ladder, prepay option) and pass to legal for a quick redline. Karthik, can you validate ramp numbers vs expected ops capacity? Camila, ping finance for invoicing cadence preference (quarterly arrears vs annual prepay).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Jenna Morris <procurement@crestline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestline.ai>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@finance.crestline.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase for Q3 rollout

Thanks for the options. Procurement/Finance's initial asks:

- Crestline prefers quarterly invoices in arrears tied to actual consumption + committed capacity billing; annual prepay is a hard sell unless there's a meaningful uplift in discount.
- Can you quantify the "one complimentary surge (48 hours)" in token terms and whether it affects committed utilization? We need clear boundaries.
- Regarding the canary: we need an SLO for failed canary fallbacks (how fast does Redwood revert and what are the communication SLAs?).
- Legal will need a clean amendment with explicit surge fees and a sample SLA clause for sustained >3x traffic for more than 14 days.

Attached are our procurement acceptance criteria and a short list of preferred invoice fields. If you can circulate a clean amendment and a short summary of runbooks for surge and canary rollback, we can route this to our legal this week.

Thanks,
Jenna Morris
Senior Procurement Manager
Crestline AI

Attachments: Crestline_Procurement_Criteria.pdf (pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Morris <procurement@crestline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crestline.ai>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@finance.crestline.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase for Q3 rollout — proposed path forward

Team —

Thanks for the clarifying asks, Jenna. Summary and proposed path:

- Commercial: proceed with Option 1 (24-month term, graduated ramp, quarterly true-ups). We'll set the discount ladder at 12% on committed tokens; annual prepay remains optional for +4% off.
- Surge: define complimentary launch surge = up to 15M tokens (48 hours) that does NOT count against committed monthly utilization; subsequent surge events billed per surge rate in the appendix.
- Canary/SLOs: 14-day canary default; automatic fallback within 10 minutes of an anomalous error-rate spike >2x baseline. Incident comms: Pager to Crestline on P1 within 5 minutes, post-mortem within 48 hours for non-trivial rollbacks.
- Billing: quarterly invoices in arrears (default). We'll include the preferred invoice fields you provided.

Next concrete steps:
- Marissa & Legal will produce a clean amendment reflecting the above and the pricing appendix.
- I will upload a DocuSign package to the HubSpot deal and share the signing link.
- Ops will share a 2-page surge/canary runbook for your engineering and SRE teams.

Estimated timeline: amendment by Tue 04/05, legal review by Crestline by Fri 04/09, signature by mid-April to make operational prep for the Q3 launch.
